source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.leaves: Thick glossy glabrous simple blades 5–12 × up to 4 cm, paler below
morphology_documented.flowers: Densely flowered axillary racemes about 3 cm; stalks 3–4 mm, sepals about 1 mm, cream petals 2–3 mm
morphology_documented.fruit: Shiny black drupes ripening in fall, often persistent
morphology_documented.habitat: Lowland settings; cultivated and escaping, historical native range primarily eastern and southeastern TX

source_scope_note: Species-level and key-level traits distinguished; modern secondary traits stay attributed to their own sources.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: The species is statewide Texas-native but many local plantings may be horticultural; no Hays county certification inferred
Historical fruit persistence and axillary racemes aid comparison with deciduous P. serotina
preservation: Additive research only, species JSON and photo/attribution/gallery assets unchanged
